correctness.rationale: The proof establishes generic hypersurface duality from Kaji (2003), proves a nonzero quadratic value on the generic radical of the odd alternating Hessian by an explicit triangle-plus-pairs specialization, and uses formal elimination to determine the complete contact algebra as \(k[[t]]/(t^2)\). An incidence-dimension comparison excludes two distinct geometric contacts for all odd r>=5; the explicit matrix-pencil discriminant does so for r=3. Consequently the function-field degree is exactly two and purely inseparable. The standalone exact checker corroborates finite cases; the infinite proof is independent of enumeration.

originality.rationale: The 2003 Kaji primary paper proves hypersurface duality and nonreflexivity for odd-dimensional Segre varieties in characteristic two and computes generic Hessian corank one; it does not state the generic conormal field degree or identify its contact scheme. The new proof adds an independent nonvanishing quadratic-radical criterion and a separate global double-contact dimension argument, giving exact inseparable degree two for every odd binary factor count. The classical characteristic-two 2x2x2 hyperdeterminant reduction is background, not independently claimed. Search is not a uniqueness proof; residual coverage risks are recorded.

value.rationale: The conormal inseparability degree is an intrinsic and motivated quantitative invariant of projective duality in positive characteristic, directly relevant to the Kleiman–Piene problem and the well-known nonreflexivity of odd-dimensional Segre products. A uniform exact degree of two, together with a complete generic contact scheme description, materially strengthens a qualitative rank criterion across an infinite natural family. It is neither an arbitrary instance nor a rebranding of the classical 2x2x2 hyperdeterminant equation.
